# run_python_skill_tool

> Run an approved, server-side Python skill by name and (if it generates a file) attach the result to the conversation.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | `data` |
| Callable | MCP clients; in-app @ai conversations; grantable to agents |
| Filter | `https://www.dsiloed.com/api/v1/mcp?tools=run_python_skill_tool` |

## Description

This is the description the server sends to the model, verbatim.

Run an approved, server-side Python skill by name and (if it generates a file)
attach the result to the conversation. Use this for capabilities that need the
Python ecosystem — e.g. generating a real PowerPoint (.pptx) deck.

Agents do NOT write Python. You invoke a pre-approved `script_id` with a
structured `params` object that matches that script's documented inputs.

AVAILABLE SCRIPTS:
- "pptx_from_outline" → generates a *designed* .pptx PowerPoint deck (themed
  colors, fonts, layout variety, charts/tables/images). params:
  {
    "title": "Deck Title",                       // required
    "subtitle": "optional subtitle",             // title-slide subtitle
    "theme": "corporate" | "dark" | "minimal",   // preset (default: corporate)
    "palette": { "primary": "#274C77", "accent": "#E5007E", ... },  // optional custom colors (hex)
    "fonts": { "heading": "Inter", "body": "Inter" },               // optional
    "footer": "Confidential",                    // optional footer on content slides
    "template_llm_file_id": 123,                 // optional: a branded .pptx LlmFile to inherit
    "slides": [                                  // required; each picks a layout:
      { "layout": "section",    "title": "Performance", "subtitle": "..." },
      { "layout": "bullets",    "title": "...", "bullets": ["a","b"], "speaker_notes": "..." },
      { "layout": "two_column", "title": "...", "columns": [ {"heading":"Risks","bullets":[...]}, {"heading":"Mitigations","bullets":[...]} ] },
      { "layout": "stat",       "title": "...", "stats": [ {"value":"+22%","label":"Revenue"} ] },   // 1-4
      { "layout": "quote",      "quote": "...", "attribution": "..." },
      { "layout": "chart",      "title": "...", "chart": {"type":"bar|line|pie","categories":["Q1","Q2"],"series":[{"name":"2026","values":[4.1,5.0]}]} },
      { "layout": "table",      "title": "...", "table": {"headers":["A","B"],"rows":[["1","2"]]} },
      { "layout": "image",      "title": "...", "image_b64": "<base64 PNG/JPG>", "caption": "..." },
      { "layout": "closing",    "title": "Thank you", "subtitle": "..." }
    ]
  }
  Notes: a title slide is added automatically from title/subtitle. Pick the
  layout that fits each slide's content. Keep bullets short (3-5). For brand
  decks, pass `template_llm_file_id` of an attached .pptx (the skill lists its
  reference files, with ids, when you load it) — the template controls the
  colours/fonts, so do NOT also pass a `palette`, and do not invent brand hex
  values. Use `palette`/`theme` only when there is no template.

- "pdf_from_markdown" → renders Markdown into a designed, print-quality PDF
  (cover page, running header/footer with page numbers, styled tables, code,
  callouts, quotes). Use this for written documents — reports, specs, briefs,
  letters, one-pagers. params:
  {
    "title": "Q3 Engineering Review",            // required (cover + header)
    "subtitle": "Platform & Reliability",        // optional cover subtitle
    "markdown": "# Overview

Body in **Markdown**...",  // required
    "author": "Russell Holmes",                  // optional (cover)
    "date": "2026-06-15",                         // optional (defaults to today)
    "theme": "corporate" | "dark" | "minimal",   // preset (default: corporate)
    "palette": { "primary": "#274C77", "secondary": "#6096BA", "accent": "#E5007E", "text": "#2D3748", "muted": "#5B6B7B", "background": "#FFFFFF", "rule": "#E2E8F0", "code_bg": "#F4F4F4" }, // optional per-key hex overrides
    "fonts": { "heading": "Inter", "body": "Inter", "mono": "JetBrains Mono" }, // optional
    "footer": "Confidential",                    // optional footer on body pages
    "cover": true,                                // optional (default true)
    "toc": false,                                 // optional table of contents
    "page_numbers": true                          // optional (default true)
  }
  Colors & fonts are fully customizable: the default `corporate` theme uses the
  PortableMind brand colors and matches the pptx deck theme. Pass `theme` to pick
  a preset, `palette` to override any individual color (merges over the theme — give
  only the keys you want to change), and `fonts` to set heading/body/mono families.
  The output carries NO logos or image branding — colors and type only.
  Markdown supports headings, lists, tables, fenced code (```lang),
  blockquotes, and callouts via admonition syntax (`!!! note "Title"`).
  EMBED AN IMAGE OR DIAGRAM: reference any image LlmFile you have (e.g. a
  diagram you just generated with diagram_from_spec as `format: "png"`) using
  the file id as the image source — `![Architecture](file:1624)`. It renders
  inline in the PDF. This is how you put a diagram INSIDE a report: first
  generate the diagram as a PNG, then embed its id here. (Only image files
  embed; the link the diagram tool returns is a click-link, not an image.)

- "diagram_from_spec" → renders a diagram (flowchart, architecture, sequence,
  ER, state, …) into a branded, on-brand image. Use this whenever the user
  asks for a diagram, chart of boxes/arrows, architecture picture, or flow —
  NOT pdf_from_markdown (Markdown can't draw a diagram). params:
  {
    "title": "Custom UI Integration",           // required (banner + filename)
    "subtitle": "On the PortableMind platform",  // optional (pdf banner)
    "engine": "mermaid",                          // "mermaid" (default) | "graphviz"
    "mermaid": "flowchart LR
  UI["Custom UI"] --> API["Agents API"] --> P["Platform"]", // required when engine=mermaid
    "dot": "UI -> API -> P;",                    // required when engine=graphviz (DOT body only)
    "rankdir": "LR",                              // optional graphviz: LR (default) | TB
    "format": "pdf",                              // "pdf" (default) | "png" | "svg"
    "theme": "corporate",                         // "corporate" (default) | "dark" | "minimal"
    "palette": { "primary": "#274C77", "accent": "#E5007E" }, // optional hex overrides
    "footer": "Confidential"                      // optional (pdf only)
  }
  Use `engine: "mermaid"` (default) for the best-looking diagrams — write plain
  Mermaid (flowchart/sequenceDiagram/erDiagram/stateDiagram/etc.) with NO
  `%%{init}%%` blocks and NO `style`/`classDef` colors; the skill owns all
  theming and branding. Use `engine: "graphviz"` only when you want deterministic
  graph layout: pass the DOT statements as `dot` (the skill adds the `digraph{}`
  wrapper, theme attrs, and rankdir) with NO color/font attributes. Default
  output is a branded PDF; pass `format` for a raw `png`/`svg`.

- "infographic_from_template" → renders a designed, on-brand INFOGRAPHIC (poster-
  style: headline, card zones, color bands, connectors, icons) from a NAMED
  template + your content. Use this for "make an infographic / a polished
  architecture or positioning graphic" — NOT diagram_from_spec (node graphs) or
  pdf_from_markdown (prose). params:
  {
    "template": "governed_core",   // governed_core|layered_stack|hub_spoke|process_flow|comparison_metrics
    "content": { ... },             // REQUIRED — must match the chosen template's content schema
    "format": "png",                // "png" (default) | "pdf"
    "theme": "corporate",           // "corporate" (default) | "dark"
    "palette": { "accent": "#E5007E" } // optional hex overrides
  }
  Pick the template whose `when_to_use` fits the request, then fill ONLY that
  template's content fields — the template owns layout, colors, connectors and
  icons (you never write HTML). Load the `infographics` skill to see each
  template's purpose, content schema, limits, and an example. Content is
  validated against the schema; oversized/missing fields error so you can retry.

- "brand_composition" → renders YOUR OWN HTML/CSS onto an EXACT-SIZE canvas with the
  workspace brand kit injected. Use this for pixel-exact marketing assets — LinkedIn
  banners, square posts, stories, OG images, ad tiles — where the copy, brand hex
  colours, logo and canvas size must be exact (image models can't do that). params:
  {
    "preset": "linkedin_banner",   // linkedin_banner 1512x256 | linkedin_banner_hq 4200x700 |
                                   // linkedin_post 1080x1080 | linkedin_post_landscape 1200x628 |
                                   // instagram_post | instagram_story 1080x1920 | facebook_cover 851x315 |
                                   // facebook_post 1200x628 | x_header 1500x500 | x_post 1600x900 |
                                   // youtube_thumbnail 1280x720 | og_image 1200x630 | profile_square 400x400 |
                                   // presentation_16_9 1920x1080 | a4_portrait | custom (+ width, height)
    "html": "<div class='hero'>…</div>",   // REQUIRED body fragment; the canvas is position:relative, exact px
    "css": ".hero{…}",                      // optional extra CSS
    "assets": { "hero": 1234 },             // LlmFile ids (images/fonts) → use as {{asset:hero}} in html/css
    "format": "png",                        // png (default) | webp | pdf
    "title": "PortableMind LinkedIn banner"
  }
  The brand kit is injected automatically as CSS variables: `--brand-<color name>`
  (e.g. var(--brand-primary), var(--brand-accent)), `--font-heading` / `--font-body` /
  `--font-mono`, and the logo as `{{brand:logo}}` (an <img src> value). Load the
  `graphics` skill to see the configured colour names. Scripts, event handlers,
  iframes and remote URLs are stripped and the renderer has NO network — inline
  everything and reference uploaded images only through `assets`. For artwork,
  FIRST call generate_image_tool (prompt with "no text"), then pass its file id as an
  asset and lay the copy over it here. Fonts available: Liberation Sans/Serif/Mono,
  DejaVu Sans/Serif — or fonts uploaded to the brand kit.

The generated file is persisted as an LlmFile and AUTOMATICALLY ATTACHED to the
tool-result message. CRITICAL: your reply to the user MUST end with the exact
markdown link this tool returns — `[Title](/app/file-artifact/file/<id>)` — on its
own line, so they can open the file. The user cannot easily find the file without
it; a reply that omits the link is incomplete.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `script_id` | string | yes | Identifier of the approved Python skill to run (e.g. "pptx_from_outline"). |
| `params` | object | no | Structured parameters for the script, matching its documented input shape. For pptx_from_outline: { title, subtitle?, slides: [{ title, bullets?, speaker_notes? }] }. |
| `directory_path` | string | no | Optional virtual directory to file the result under (e.g. "/decks/2026"). If omitted, the file lands in a predictable per-type folder: "/skills/pptx" for PowerPoint decks, "/skills/pdf" for PDFs, "/skills/xlsx" for spreadsheets. Only set this when the user asks for a specific location. Regenerating is always safe — a same-named file is auto-versioned ("Title (2)"), never overwritten or blocked. |
